author: terencechain
content: Short answer: it doesn't really know. Prysm has a single `connectedETH1` bool. It gets set true when the startup dial succeeds and `eth_chainId` returns the right chain, and it only gets set false on startup retry or shutdown. Nothing in running state changes that. Engine API results don't change it at all, so a failing `newPayload` or `FCU` has no effect on what `/eth/v1/node/syncing` reports as el_offline. That's why our nethermind nodes said el_offline=false for the whole 10 mins the engine port was refusing connections. The snooper makes it a bit worse. Prysm never sees connection refused, it sees a 200 level TCP connect and then an HTTP 500 with a JSON body from the proxy. Our engine client can't map that to a payload status, so it becomes "undefined execution engine error" and the envelope gets dropped

content:
<@755590043632140352> my ai said this
```
Prysm skips its PTC vote when the envelope lands between 6s and 9s. The availability event wakes the VC, the BN answers Unavailable because it is before the deadline and the payload is
     not timely, and SubmitPayloadAttestation returns without retrying at 9s. That is exactly the window a withholding builder would target, so Prysm's PTC share goes silent in the
     scenario PTC exists for. Fix is either a retry at the deadline in the VC or having the BN endpoint wait until the deadline instead of erroring. Worth telling potuz
```

author: nflaig
content:
<@654267572107083777> that's why nimbus availability vote is wrong, we saw that before
```
Nimbus casts the absent vote at 6s with a possibly stale blob flag. It gives up at PAYLOAD_DUE rather than the PTC deadline and evaluates blob_data_available then. Columns arriving
     between 6s and 9s make that flag wrong. Waiting until 9s for the absent vote costs nothing, since payload_present cannot flip after 6s.
```
